notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide and docs/evidence/otp.md at 622cd82. The guide's Sources note was checked on 17 October 2026 on the 16 October build (mirror v0.1.78-a116616, the #274 fix), so items citing it carry that build. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). GitHub's compare of v0.1.78-a116616 and v0.1.78-dbe0e02 changes no OTP, SupportText, Button, token or typography file, so the build the guide was checked on and the installed one render OTP the same. Its OTP.tsx still matches every guide sentence used here, read from source, not run: length defaults to 6; one hidden number-pad TextInput (1 px, transparent) takes the typing and the slots only display it; slots are flex 1 1 0 with a 48 px maximum (pinSlot/width) and a hard-coded 8 px gap, in a row that starts at the left, inside 8 px padding, so the OTP fills its container (width 100%) and slots shrink in a narrow one; filled slots and the focused active slot light their underline (fade in 120 ms, out 220 ms) and a caret blinks in the active slot; isInvalid snaps every underline to the error colour; the support area shows, in order, the error (errorMessage, or supportText promoted to Error), then the resend countdown, then supportText, and the support row is right-aligned and lets long text shrink and wrap (the #274 fix); resend counts down (“Resend OTP in Ns”, default 30 s, Loading status), then shows a small Resend Button (Neutral, S, Low) that reads “Sending…” while onResend runs, then counts down again; isDisabled sets 40% opacity and makes the field not editable; enableSmsAutofill (default true) sets the native one-time-code autofill hints. No guide sentence is contradicted. #178 (slots never shrink, 7–8 digits wider than a phone) is Done and published (636f3f5, 8 October), and the guide no longer uses the FitWidth docs wrapper; the evidence's 1 October lines that say slots never shrink, that the OTP hugs its slots, and that codes longer than 6 digits are too wide (its Rendered and Limits sections, on 0.1.77) are out of date and were not used, nor was the 8 October line that the support line moved to the left (#210, fixed 13 October). Not recorded: allowedPattern, autoFocus, style, the resend config's formatCountdown, labels and resendButtonModes, and the OTPResend and useOtpResend exports, which the guide and evidence keep out of the designer guide; Color Mode, which the building rules leave to the device. Accessibility: the guide says nothing; the one item rests on the evidence's 1 October render on 0.1.77 (the hidden field's name, “OTP input, N digits”, and the disabled marking), which the installed source still sets (the hidden TextInput's accessibilityLabel, and disabled on the root Pressable), so it carries that version and is flagged. It says only what that render shows: the evidence does not record what a screen reader announces. Content bad is empty: the Don't “Write the timer as text” shows “Didn’t get it? Resend in 30s”, which is bad as a static timer, not as wording, so it is recorded as a configuration rule instead. avoidWhen is empty: the guide says what OTP is for but never when not to use it; its Don'ts are configurations, recorded under configuration. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every OTP and on the In context Card, VStack and Text) and no other modes. The In context example repeats the guide's composition (Card, VStack, two Text lines and the OTP; Text takes its words through text) with the screen's state reduced to an empty code and no error; the other two are the guide's Invalid and Disabled cards, with its own code and lines (the schema allows three examples). Left out of examples: the docs host wrapper, the playground, the In context status readout (plain page copy), and the three Don'ts. Refreshed 29 October 2026 for guide fix #543 (3f56271): the evidence now calls the ready Resend control a Button; the resend fact (/facts/props, resend) quotes the new sentence.

examples.purpose: Verifying a phone number, the guide's In context: a Card with a heading line, a line saying where the code went, and a 6-digit OTP with a 30-second resend timer. The screen keeps the code (value and onChange), checks it when the last digit is entered (onComplete), and sets isInvalid; errorMessage then replaces the timer.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <Text text="Verify your number" />
    <Text text="We sent a 6-digit code to your phone." />
    <OTP
      value=""
      onChange={() => {}}
      onComplete={() => {}}
      isInvalid={false}
      errorMessage="Incorrect code. Try again."
      resend={{ durationSeconds: 30, onResend: () => {} }}
    />
  </VStack>
</Card>
